content.title: Hidden Amal: The Real Reason Behind the Loss of Tawfiq!
content.subtitle: How we unknowingly lose some of our most precious treasures.
content.body:
Just as people keep their most valuable possessions hidden in the deepest corners of a safe, a believer's voluntary acts of worship should remain hidden from the eyes of the world.

Whether you wake up late at night for Tahajjud, recite a few pages of the Quran every day, or quietly engage in Dhikr, keep these deeds between yourself and the Master of the Throne.

Should All Acts of Worship Be Hidden?

Islam does not ask us to hide every act of worship. The five daily obligatory prayers in congregation, Friday prayers, and collective acts of worship like Zakat are performed openly to create a religious atmosphere in society.

The Holy Quran beautifully explains this balance:

"If you give charity openly, it is good. But if you give it secretly and give it to the poor, that is better for you. Through this, Allah will erase some of your sins." (Surah Al-Baqarah: 271)

The Social Media Trap and the Quiet Satisfaction of the Ego

Today, social media has become one of the biggest places where our private good deeds lose their secrecy. Many of us record moments of worship, charity, or helping others and share them online.

Perhaps you began with sincere love and the intention of pleasing Allah. But when your video goes viral, the comments fill with praise, and likes and shares pour in, ask yourself: deep down, don't you feel a little sense of self-satisfaction?

And the most frightening consequence is that, gradually, you may lose the tawfiq to perform that very deed again!

An Amazing Example from the Salaf

Imagine having deeds witnessed only by the Master of the Throne. Our righteous predecessors, the Salaf, performed obligatory worship with others but kept their voluntary deeds even more hidden than their sins.

The renowned Tabi'i Ayyub As-Sakhtiyani (RA) would spend the night weeping in Tahajjud. When Fajr approached, he would clear his throat as if to make the people in the next room believe he had only just woken up!

Another great Tabi'i, Dawud ibn Abi Hind (RA), fasted voluntarily for 40 consecutive years without even his family knowing. Every morning, he would leave for the market carrying his lunch and give it to someone in need along the way. His family thought he had eaten at the market, while the people at the market thought he had eaten at home!

Deeds Meant to Remain Between You and Allah

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave glad tidings about seven categories of people who will find shelter under Allah's Throne on the Day of Judgment. One of them is:

“A person who gives charity so secretly that their left hand does not know what their right hand has spent.”

Let us start building some private acts of worship today, deeds that no one in this world will witness: no friend, no family member, and no social media audience.

Let tonight's Tahajjud, today's Quran recitation, or the story of helping someone in need remain between you and your Lord. When all worldly accounts come to an end, these hidden deeds will become the light that brightens the darkness of your grave, In Sha Allah.

References:

  1. The virtue of open and hidden deeds: Al-Quran, Surah Al-Baqarah (Verse 271)

  2. The reward for hidden deeds (shade of the Throne): Sahih al-Bukhari (Hadith 660)

  3. The account of Ayyub As-Sakhtiyani (RA): Siyar A'lam al-Nubala (Imam Adh-Dhahabi)

  4. The account of Dawud ibn Abi Hind's 40 years of fasting: Hilyat al-Awliya (Abu Nu'aym al-Isfahani)
